lines.text: Do you know how fingerprints work? Those tiny ridges formed before you were born, and no two people share them. Not even identical twins.
The ridges carry sweat and oil, so everything you touch keeps a faint copy of the pattern.
Detectives brush on a fine powder. It sticks to the oil, and the print appears.
Experts don't compare the whole picture. They look for tiny details, where ridges end, or split in two.
Your phone's sensor does something similar. The ridges touch it, the valleys don't, and it maps the difference.
Sometimes you'd rather leave no trace. Orbi's Anonymous mode has no profile, no name, no GPS. Just a throwaway ID that's gone when you leave.
